hook.line: Walk down the block in La Candelaria and *se* is everywhere: on the signs, in the gossip, in everyone's morning. It's the same little word doing three different jobs.
hook.es: En el café se come muy bien.
hook.en: You eat really well at the café.

examples.es: Vale se levanta a las cuatro.
Hernando se sienta siempre en la misma mesa.
examples.en: Hernando always sits at the same table.

examples.es: Tomás y Vale se conocieron en el café.
examples.en: Tomás and Vale met at the café.

examples.es: Rosa y Hernando se querían mucho.
examples.en: Rosa and Hernando loved each other very much.

rule:
Ask one question: who is doing it, and to whom?

One person, doing it to themselves: *Vale se levanta.* Vale gets (herself) up. This is your daily routine *se*.

Two or more people, doing it to each other: *Tomás y Vale se conocieron.* They met each other. The verb is plural and there's a pair or a group.

Nobody named at all: *Se arrienda apartamento.* Somebody is renting it out, and it doesn't matter who. English says for rent, is spoken, or you (*Aquí se come bien*: you eat well here).

So look for the person. A name with a singular verb: themselves. A pair with a plural verb and a relationship verb (*conocerse*, *quererse*, *ayudarse*): each other. No person anywhere: people in general.
smallPrint: Teachers call these the reflexive *se*, the reciprocal *se* and the impersonal *se*.

readAndPick.es: Vale se levanta a las cuatro.
options: Vale and someone get each other up at four.

readAndPick.es: Tomás y Vale se conocieron en el café.
options: Tomás and Vale met at the café.
Tomás met Vale's family at the café.
They rent each other an apartment.
He talks to himself in English here.
They talk to each other in English here.

readAndPick.es: Rosa y Hernando se querían mucho.
options: Rosa and Hernando loved each other very much.

readAndPick.es: Hernando se sienta siempre en la misma mesa.
options: People always sit at the same table.
Hernando always sits at the same table.
He lives with himself in Bogotá.
They live with each other in Bogotá.
Vale and Tomás help each other.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *conocieron* or *se conocieron* and type the whole sentence: *Rosa y Hernando ___ en el café.* (Rosa and Hernando met at the café.)
yourTurn.answer: Rosa y Hernando se conocieron en el café.
accept: Hernando y Rosa se conocieron en el café.
yourTurn.why: They met each other: a pair, a plural verb and *se*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *se levanta* or *levanta* and type the whole sentence: *Vale ___ a las cuatro.*
yourTurn.answer: Vale se levanta a las cuatro.
yourTurn.why: One person getting herself up: the routine *se*.

yourTurn.prompt: Write the sign in Spanish: House for sale.
yourTurn.why: No seller named, so *se* + the verb for he or she.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: English is spoken here.
yourTurn.why: Nobody in particular speaks it, so *se habla*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Hernando always sits at the same table.
yourTurn.answer: Hernando se sienta siempre en la misma mesa.
accept: Hernando siempre se sienta en la misma mesa.
yourTurn.why: One person, sitting himself down: routine *se*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about two people who love each other: *Rosa quería mucho a Hernando.*
yourTurn.answer: Rosa y Hernando se querían mucho.
accept: Hernando y Rosa se querían mucho.
yourTurn.why: Two people, a plural verb and *se*: they loved each other.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about people in general: *Comemos muy bien en el café.* (You eat really well at the café.)
yourTurn.answer: En el café se come muy bien.
accept: Se come muy bien en el café.
yourTurn.why: Nobody named: *se* + the verb for he or she.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Nobody is named, so the verb stays in the he or she form.

pitfalls.wrong: Tomás y Vale conocieron en el café.
pitfalls.right: Tomás y Vale se conocieron en el café.
pitfalls.why: Met each other needs *se*; without it, they met someone else.
English says is spoken; Spanish uses *se* with the he or she form instead.

personal: Write three short lines about your world: one thing you do to yourself every morning, one person you met (*Nos conocimos...*), and one thing people do where you live (*Aquí se...*).
